questions.q: What kind of exercise is enterprise structure design, before any setup task is opened?
options: A planning exercise, driven by legal, currency, and reporting questions
A purely technical database exercise
An exercise with no effect on later configuration
A configuration exercise only
questions.explain: Design starts by answering questions about legal entities, countries, currencies, and reporting needs, before any configuration begins.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the core design questions this lesson lists?
options: How many different functional or reporting currencies are involved?
What color scheme should the Oracle Fusion home page use?
How many legally registered companies does the business operate as?
In how many countries, with how many statutory requirements?
questions.explain: The design questions concern legal entities, countries, currencies, and reporting needs — not cosmetic UI preferences.

questions.q: What is the guiding principle this lesson recommends for enterprise structure complexity?
options: Complexity should be added at random to test the system
Always build the maximum number of ledgers and charts of accounts possible
Start with the simplest structure that satisfies today's legal, tax, and reporting requirements
Never create more than one legal entity under any circumstances
questions.explain: The lesson's guiding principle is to default to the simplest structure that meets real, current requirements, adding complexity only when genuinely needed.

questions.q: Why is over-engineering enterprise structures (extra ledgers or charts of accounts 'just in case') a problem?
options: Oracle Fusion technically limits you to one structure anyway
It has no cost since storage is unlimited
It is not a problem; more structures are always safer
Every extra structure must be configured, maintained, and reconciled indefinitely
questions.explain: Each additional structure adds ongoing configuration, maintenance, and reconciliation burden, which is why simpler designs are generally preferred.

questions.q: What can happen when legal (statutory) reporting needs and management reporting needs point in different directions?
options: Oracle Fusion has no way to address this at all
The structure that satisfies statutory reporting may differ from how management wants to view results, requiring tools like hierarchies or secondary ledgers
The legal entity must always be eliminated
This situation never occurs in practice
questions.explain: Legal and management reporting needs can diverge, and Oracle Fusion offers tools such as segment hierarchies and secondary ledgers to address exactly this tension.
